Final Project – Harmonic Analysis on Grid-connected Bridge Inverter (with Unipolar Modulation)

Author

Qiaoxuan Zhang

Published

June 30, 2026

Objective

The objective of this experiment is to design, implement, and analyse a single-phase full-bridge inverter in MATLAB/Simulink using unipolar sinusoidal pulse-width modulation (SPWM). Specifically, the report aims to:

  1. Build and verify the Simulink model with a resistive load, both without and with a filter inductor \(L_f\).
  2. Examine the inverter output voltage \(V_{ab}\) on the resistive load and its Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectrum under both conditions.
  3. Evaluate the voltage waveform across the resistive load and its Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) when \(L_f\) is present.
  4. Compare the harmonic performance of unipolar SPWM against square wave modulation.
  5. Extend the model to grid-connected operation and verify the steady-state phasor relationship between the inverter output voltage, the filter inductor voltage, and the grid voltage.
  6. Measure the grid current waveform and its THD.

Key simulation parameters are summarised in Table 1.

Simulink Model — Unipolar SPWM with Resistive Load

The single-phase full-bridge inverter consists of four IGBT/diode pairs (S1–S4) connected in two legs. In unipolar SPWM, the two legs are controlled by independent sinusoidal references compared against a shared high-frequency triangular sequence. The resulting three-level output voltage \(V_{ab}\) switches among \(+V_{dc}\), \(0\), and \(-V_{dc}\), pushing the dominant harmonic content to sidebands around \(2f_{s}\).

Without Filter Inductor

In this configuration the filter inductor is not included and only a resistive load is connected between the bridge midpoints. This allows the raw, unfiltered \(V_{ab}\) waveform to be captured for FFT analysis.

With Filter Inductor (\(L_f\) in circuit)

The filter inductor \(L_f\) is connected in series to the resistive load. The voltage scope is placed to measure the waveform output of the actual load voltage after filtering.

Output Voltage Waveform and FFT Analysis

Without Filter Inductor

Without \(L_f\), the bridge output voltage \(V_{ab}\) is a three-level switching waveform.

The FFT analysis shows dominant harmonics at 60 Hz and \(1000 \pm 60\;\mathrm{Hz}\). The THD level is approximately 52.3%, a relatively high value due to the presence of low-order harmonics.

With Filter Inductor

With \(L_f\) reconnected, the inductor acts as a low-pass filter and attenuates the high-frequency harmonic content. The load voltage across \(R\) approaches a sinusoidal waveform.

The FFT analysis confirms that the dominant harmonic content has been shifted to higher frequencies, with the THD reduced to a much lower value of about 9%, indicating effective filtering.

Comparison with Square Wave Modulation

To benchmark harmonic performance, the gate-signal generator was replaced with a simple square-wave source operating at the fundamental frequency \(f_1\). In this scheme, S1 and S4 conduct simultaneously during the positive half-cycle while S2 and S3 conduct during the negative half-cycle, producing a two-level output (\(+V_{dc}\) / \(-V_{dc}\)) with no carrier modulation, as shown in Figure 7 on the left side.

The output voltage waveform is a simple square wave, and the FFT spectrum shows significant low-order harmonic content, with the harmonics of 60 Hz, 180 Hz, 300 Hz, etc., corresponding to 1st, 3rd, 5th, etc. harmonics of the fundamental frequency. The THD is approximately 48.3%, which is higher than that of unipolar SPWM with filtering.

Simulink Model — Grid-Connected Operation

In the grid-connected configuration the resistive load is replaced by an AC grid voltage source \(V_g\) connected through the filter inductor \(L_f\). The inverter must synthesise an output voltage \(V_{ab}\) whose amplitude and phase are determined by the grid voltage and the desired injected current.

Steady-State Phasor Analysis

The KVL equation around the output loop (Figure 10) gives:

\[ V_{ab} = V_L + V_g \tag{1}\]

where \(V_L = j\omega I_{L_f} L_f\) is the phasor voltage across the filter inductor.

With the grid current \(I_{L_f} = 1\angle 0°\;\mathrm{A}\) (amplitude, taken as the reference phasor) and the circuit parameters in Table 1, the inductor voltage is:

\[ V_L = j\omega L_f \, I_{L_f} = j \underbrace{(120\pi)}_{\omega} \times \underbrace{(10 \times 10^{-3})}_{L_f} \times 1 \approx 3.77\angle 90°\;\text{V} \tag{2}\]

The grid voltage phasor (in phase with \(I_{L_f}\) for a resistive grid equivalent) is:

\[ V_g = 120\sqrt{2} \approx 169.68\angle 0°\;\text{V} \tag{3}\]

Because \(V_L \perp V_g\) in the phasor diagram (Figure 11), the required inverter output amplitude is:

\[ V_{ab} = \sqrt{V_L^2 + V_g^2} = \sqrt{3.77^2 + 169.68^2} = \sqrt{14.21 + 28\,791.38} \approx 169.722\;\text{V} \tag{4}\]

The corresponding phase lead of \(V_{ab}\) over \(V_g\) is:

\[ \theta = \arctan\!\left(\frac{V_L}{V_g}\right) = \arctan\!\left(\frac{3.77}{169.68}\right) \approx 0.0222\;\text{rad} \equiv 1.2728° \tag{5}\]

Finally, the modulation index required to produce this output from a \(V_{dc} = 200\;\text{V}\) DC bus is:

\[ \boxed{m_a = \frac{|V_{ab}|}{V_{dc}} = \frac{169.722}{200} \approx 0.84861} \tag{6}\]

Simulink Model Screenshots

The sinusoidal reference amplitude and phase offset were set in the unipolar SPWM subsystem (top-left in Figure 12) to match the phasor analysis results in Steady-State Phasor Analysis. The current measurement block was placed in series with \(L_f\) to probe the grid current waveform.

Waveforms were captured from the current scope, showing the grid current \(i_g(t)\) in phase with the grid voltage \(V_g\) for unity power-factor injection. The THD of the grid current was measured to be approximately 13%, indicating that the inverter is effectively injecting a nearly sinusoidal current into the grid.

Conclusion

This report demonstrated the simulation of a single-phase grid-connected full-bridge inverter using unipolar SPWM in MATLAB/Simulink. The inverter was first tested with a resistive load, both without and with a filter inductor \(L_f\). The FFT analysis confirmed that the filter effectively reduced the THD of the load voltage from 52.3% to 9%. Compared to square-wave switching, unipolar SPWM produced a three-level output voltage with dominant harmonics shifted to higher frequencies, producing a unfiltered THD of 48.3%.

The phasor analysis in Steady-State Phasor Analysis showed that the inverter output voltage \(V_{ab}\) must lead the grid voltage \(V_g\) by a small angle \(\theta \approx 1.2728°\) to drive the desired grid current \(I_{L_f}\). The required modulation index was calculated to be approximately \(0.84861\). The Simulink model for grid-connected operation confirmed that the grid current waveform was approximately sinusoidal and in phase with the grid voltage, with a THD of about 13%, indicating effective harmonic performance.
